correlation_pearson.title: Pearson correlation
correlation_pearson.summary: Explore the strength and direction of a linear relationship between numerical measurements.
correlation_pearson.why: You have paired numerical measurements from independent items and want a symmetric measure of association, without choosing one variable as the response.

availability.note: Stable module listed on 29 October 2026. Correlation controls checked against the released v0.96.0 interface; the examples have not been run in desktop JASP.

setup.title: Assign the measurements
setup.text: Move Roughness_um and Bond_strength_N to Variables. Each row must pair measurements from the same component. Leave Part out of the analysis.

setup.title: Choose the coefficient and uncertainty
setup.text: Select Pearson's r. Under Additional Options, select Confidence intervals and Sample size. Keep Correlated for a two-sided hypothesis unless a directional question was prespecified. These intervals describe the correlation coefficient; the separate interval option under Scatter plots draws a band around a regression line.

setup.title: Inspect the relationship
setup.text: Select Scatter plots; inspect curvature, unusual points, and distinct subgroups. When exploring many measurements, the Heatmap is an overview, and the pairwise plots are needed to assess what the coefficients describe.

columns.name: Part
columns.description: Identifier of the independently sampled component; do not assign it as a measured variable.

columns.name: Bond_strength_N
columns.description: Measured pull strength on the same component, in newtons.

columns.name: Coating_um
columns.description: Coating thickness, available for a separate partial-correlation question.

checks: Retain the row-level pairing and check independence between components. Repeated readings of one component need a design-specific analysis.
Pearson's r summarizes linear association. A value near zero does not rule out a curved relationship; a high value does not establish measurement agreement.

Standard Pearson inference assumes an appropriate sampling model, usually independent pairs from a bivariate-normal population. Inspect influential points and the joint pattern; a normality-test p-value alone is not a decision rule.
Check missing-value handling. Exclude cases pairwise can use different items for different correlations; report the sample size for each pair. Many exploratory tests create a multiplicity issue.
Association does not show that changing roughness would cause strength to change. Process mixtures and other common causes can produce a correlation.
report: The pair of measurements, Pearson's r, its confidence interval, the number of complete pairs, and the scatter plot.
The sampling unit, any excluded observations or missingness, and the limits of an observational interpretation.

example.title: Are roughness and bond strength related?
example.story: Eighty synthetic components each have a roughness, pull-strength, and coating-thickness measurement. Start with the roughness–strength scatter plot.
instructions: Import the CSV; set the three measured quantities to Scale and Part to Nominal.
Assign Roughness_um and Bond_strength_N to Variables. Select Pearson's r, Additional Options > Confidence intervals, Sample size, and Scatter plots.
Then add Coating_um to Variables to see all three pairwise relationships. This is a different question from partialling it out.

correlation_rank.title: Spearman or Kendall rank correlation
correlation_rank.summary: Explore a monotonic association using the order of numerical or ordered measurements.
correlation_rank.why: Your question concerns whether larger values of one measurement tend to go with larger or smaller values of another. An ordered rating or a curved monotonic pattern can be described using ranks.

availability.note: Stable module listed on 29 October 2026. Spearman and Kendall controls checked against released v0.96.0 source; the examples have not been run in desktop JASP.

setup.title: Preserve meaningful numerical ordering
setup.text: Use numeric codes in the intended order for Severity_score: 1 through 5. The verified Correlation dialog accepts numeric Scale columns; set the numeric coded column to Scale for assignment, while interpreting it as ordered and selecting a rank coefficient.

setup.title: Select a rank coefficient
setup.text: Move Roughness_um and Severity_score to Variables. Clear Pearson's r and select Spearman's rho. Kendall's tau-b is a useful alternative based on concordant and discordant pairs, with an adjustment for ties; choose and report the coefficient deliberately.

setup.title: Examine the pattern
setup.text: Under Additional Options, request Confidence intervals and Sample size; also select Scatter plots. The released calculation code provides intervals for the selected Spearman or Kendall coefficient. Points align at the five score levels; inspect monotonicity and possible product or batch mixtures.

columns.name: Part
columns.description: A different sampled item in each row.

columns.name: Roughness_um
columns.description: Measured roughness on that item, in micrometres.

columns.name: Severity_score
columns.description: Numeric codes for an ordered 1–5 rating. Assign as numeric in the Correlation dialog; interpret using a rank coefficient.

checks: Ranking does not repair dependence, a poorly sampled population, or a mixture of incompatible processes.
A monotonic relationship can be curved but should have a consistent direction. A U-shaped relationship may have a small rank correlation despite a strong association.
Ties are expected for a short rating scale. Kendall's tau-b accounts for ties; Spearman and Kendall coefficients have different interpretations and are not numerically interchangeable.

Rank confidence intervals are approximate. Additional Options > Confidence intervals refers to the coefficient; the interval option under Scatter plots instead describes a regression line. Optional From … bootstraps requests a percentile bootstrap interval; report the method and number of resamples when using it.
A rank association is not rater agreement or a causal effect. For agreement between inspectors, use the measurement-systems route.
report: The rating scale and ordering, selected coefficient (Spearman's rho or Kendall's tau-b), estimate with its confidence interval, number of complete pairs, and the observed pattern.
Any hypothesis-test method or interval actually produced by the installed JASP analysis, and the exploratory or confirmatory purpose.

example.title: Do rougher parts receive worse visual ratings?
example.story: Seventy-two synthetic parts have roughness measurements and ordered visual-severity ratings. The rating has five levels, so many values are tied.
instructions: Import the CSV and assign the numeric Roughness_um and Severity_score columns to Variables.
Select Spearman's rho and clear Pearson's r. Request Additional Options > Confidence intervals, Sample size, and Scatter plots.
Optionally inspect Kendall's tau-b as a second description. Explain why its numerical value need not equal Spearman's rho.

correlation_partial.title: Partial Pearson correlation
correlation_partial.summary: Describe the linear association between two measurements after adjusting each for specified continuous covariates.
correlation_partial.why: You want a symmetric adjusted association between two numerical variables, and a linear adjustment for the selected covariates is meaningful for your study.

availability.note: Stable module listed on 29 October 2026. Partial out controls checked against released v0.96.0 source; the examples have not been run in desktop JASP.

setup.title: Separate the pair from the adjustment variables
setup.text: Move Roughness_um and Bond_strength_N to Variables. Move Coating_um to Partial out. Select Pearson's r. The partial correlation relates the residuals after linearly regressing each measured variable on the adjustment variable.

setup.title: Request estimates and plots
setup.text: Under Additional Options, select Confidence intervals and also tick From … bootstraps; for example, use 5000 resamples. The verified released interface requires bootstrapping for partial-correlation intervals; ticking Confidence intervals alone does not produce an analytic interval. Request Sample size and Scatter plots. The partial scatter-plot axes represent adjusted residuals.

setup.title: Make the adjustment explicit
setup.text: Compare with the unadjusted Pearson correlation and report the chosen covariates. Choose covariates from the process question and study design rather than selecting those that produce a preferred result.

columns.name: Part
columns.description: Independent component identifier; exclude from the variable and adjustment boxes.

columns.name: Roughness_um
columns.description: First measurement in the adjusted association.

columns.name: Bond_strength_N
columns.description: Second measurement, paired on the same component.

columns.name: Coating_um
columns.description: Continuous covariate for the linear adjustment; assign to Partial out.

checks: Independent sampling, meaningful numerical scales, suitable linear adjustments, and appropriate residual behaviour are still needed.
Partialling out a variable does not guarantee control of confounding. Adjusting for a consequence of the variables, a collider, or a poorly measured covariate can change the interpretation adversely.

A categorical group should not be assigned arbitrary numeric codes and treated as a continuous adjustment. Use an appropriately coded regression model when factors, interactions, or nonlinear adjustments are needed.
Document missingness and the complete observations used by the partial analysis. Extra covariates reduce the information available for inference.
This method estimates an adjusted association. Causal effects require additional assumptions or a suitable experiment.

The bootstrap resamples rows and relies on independent sampled components. Report the percentile-bootstrap method and number of resamples, and check any warnings or unstable intervals; bootstrapping does not fix dependent observations or an ill-conditioned adjustment model.
report: The unadjusted and partial Pearson coefficients, their intervals and interval methods, the number of observations, and every adjustment variable. For the partial interval, report the number of bootstrap resamples.
The rationale for adjustment, plots of the residual relationship, and the limits of a causal interpretation.

example.title: Does the relationship persist after allowing for coating?
example.story: In the same 80-component synthetic example, coating thickness relates to both roughness and strength. Examine the association remaining after linear adjustment for thickness.
instructions: Move Roughness_um and Bond_strength_N to Variables; move Coating_um to Partial out.
Select Pearson's r. Under Additional Options, select Confidence intervals and From … bootstraps (for example, 5000 resamples); also request Sample size and Scatter plots.
Compare with the unadjusted coefficient. The generating model is known for this teaching example; in real observations, adjustment requires substantive justification.
